title: Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Planning

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed colorectal cancer: urgent referral criteria, staging work-up, MDT treatment planning for colon and rectal cancer, adjuvant therapy, and follow-up. Verified against the Saudi Oncology Society colorectal cancer guideline (2014), NICE NG151 and NICE NG12; capecitabine dosing from the FDA label.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: SOS guideline is 2014 — newer systemic agents may be available

pathophysiology.summary: Colorectal adenocarcinoma usually develops from adenomatous polyps. Stage (depth of invasion, nodes, metastases) and mismatch repair (MMR) status guide surgery and adjuvant treatment. Colorectal cancer is the most common cancer in Saudi men (SOS 2014).
keyMechanisms: Chromosomal instability or MMR deficiency drive progression from adenoma to cancer.
Lymph node involvement (stage III) is the main indication for adjuvant chemotherapy.
Rectal cancer is treated differently because of pelvic recurrence risk — MRI staging and preoperative (chemo)radiotherapy.

symptoms: Rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, abdominal pain, weight loss, tiredness from anaemia.
Obstruction or perforation in advanced disease.
physicalSigns: Abdominal or rectal mass; pallor; hepatomegaly.
redFlags: Large bowel obstruction — stent or surgery (NICE NG151 1.3.1–1.3.2)
FIT 10 µg Hb/g or more, rectal mass — suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: CT and colonoscopy to exclude cancer.
Do not attribute bleeding without assessment.

ruleIn.testName: CEA, FBC, liver and renal function
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Baseline for follow-up; anaemia needs correction.
ruleIn.normalValue: CEA below about 5 µg/L (laboratory dependent); Hb within reference range

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: Use NICE NG12 1.3.1–1.3.5 criteria (FIT 10 µg Hb/g or more, rectal mass).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage and MDT
actions: Complete the SOS pre-treatment evaluation; discuss all cases at a colorectal MDT (SOS).

clinicalManagement.title: Colon cancer
actions: Resection by site with 5 cm margins; laparoscopic equal to open (SOS 4.1.1).
Stage I: no adjuvant therapy. Stage II average risk: none. Stage II high risk: dMMR observe; pMMR capecitabine or 5-FU/leucovorin for 6 months (SOS 4.1.2–4.1.4).
Stage III: NICE NG151 1.3.18 — CAPOX 3 months, or FOLFOX 3–6 months, or single-agent fluoropyrimidine 6 months. SOS: FOLFOX 6 months or XELOX 8 cycles.

clinicalManagement.title: Rectal cancer
actions: Total mesorectal excision by a colorectal surgeon (SOS 4.2.1).
cT3–4 or node-positive: preoperative chemoradiotherapy, surgery 6–8 weeks later (SOS 4.2.3; NICE 1.3.5).
Early rectal cancer (cT1–T2 N0): no preoperative radiotherapy outside trials (NICE 1.3.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Advanced or metastatic
actions: Liver- or lung-only metastases: consider resection (SOS 4.3.1.2).
Palliative chemotherapy choice by performance status and RAS status (SOS 4.3.2); MSI-high/dMMR immunotherapy options (NICE 1.5).

learningObjectives: Diagnose, stage and plan treatment for colorectal cancer.

keyPoints: Colonoscopy, CT, CEA; MRI for rectal cancer.
pitfalls: Missing synchronous tumours — always full colonoscopy.
Treating rectal cancer without MRI staging.

patientEducation: Explain staging, treatment options and stoma possibilities.
lifestyleAndDiet: Physical activity and nutrition support during and after treatment.
mdtReferrals: Colorectal MDT; stoma nurse; genetics if dMMR or young onset.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: SOS: examination and CEA every 6 months for 5 years; CT yearly for 3 years if node positive; colonoscopy within 6 months if not done preoperatively, then at 3 years, then 5-yearly. NICE NG151 1.6.1: CEA and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for the first 3 years.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: CAPOX 3 months; or FOLFOX 3–6 months; or fluoropyrimidine 6 months

regimens.indication: Adjuvant single-agent therapy (stage III colon; or stage II high-risk pMMR per SOS)
adjustments: Test for DPYD variants before starting (label boxed warning)
Renal impairment: dose modification per label Section 2
Combination regimens (CAPOX, FOLFOX) dosed by oncology protocol — not reproduced
monitoring: FBC, renal function, hand-foot syndrome, diarrhoea each cycle
